question: Who wrote the book of Romans?

retrieved.section: Romans 12 has the fourth “therefore” in Romans
retrieved.text:
Romans 12 has the fourth “therefore” in Romans
    - Romans 3:20 is the “therefore” of condemnation - the whole world is guilty before God
    - Romans 5:1 is the “therefore” of justification
    - Romans 8:1 is the “therefore” of assurance
    - Romans 12:1 is the “therefore” of dedication
        - The basis for the other relationships that the author discussed in this section

retrieved.section: Commentary Used: Wiersbe commentary — Romans 8 covers four spiritual freedoms:
retrieved.text:
Commentary Used: Wiersbe commentary
Romans 8 covers four spiritual freedoms:
    - 8:1-4 - Freedom from Judgment (No condemnation)
    - 8:5-17 - Freedom from Defeat (No obligation; because we cannot save ourselves, submit to God)
    - 8:18-30 - Freedom from Discouragement (No Frustration)
    - 8:31-39 (No Separation)

Loving participation
    - Attitude matters
    - Love is the circulatory system of the spiritual body
        - Have it be an honest love, not hypocritical love, humble and not proud
        - Romans 12:12 - Be JOYFUL in hope, PATIENT in affliction, and FAITHFUL in prayer
        - Share the burdens of others

retrieved.section: Romans 8:18-30 discusses suffering and pain, and how we are now free from discouragement > Three groans are mentioned > Holy Spirit groans (23-30) > The Spirit groans, but also prays on our behalf - ACTION
retrieved.text:
The Spirit groans, but also prays on our behalf - ACTION
    - We do not know God’s will or what to pray for, but the Spirit intercedes for us to “share the burden”. We are not only called to suffer with with Him, He shares our burden
